🎯 Learning Objectives

To discuss the connection between food and culture and justify opinions.
To understand a text about eating out in Britain.
To use food-tourism vocabulary in meaningful contexts.
To compare dishes, interpret information and write a recipe.

1. Speaking · Food and Culture

Brainstorm in pairs. Food and culture have a vital link that is both emotional and practical. Do you agree that food and culture go together? Bring arguments.

Think

What traditional dish represents your family or country?

Explain

Why do people cook special meals at celebrations?

Compare

Can food help travellers understand another culture?

I agree that food and culture are closely connected. Traditional dishes tell us about a country's history and customs. For example, families often prepare special food for important celebrations.

8. Speaking · Food Brands and Advertising

Brainstorm in small groups. What famous American food brands do you know? Advertising for food products is a huge business in the US. Do you agree or disagree? Explain your answer.

Discuss

Which advertisements attract young people? How?

Evaluate

Can food advertising influence our choices?

Challenge

Give one argument for and one against advertising.

Food advertising is a huge business because large brands reach millions of customers. However, some advertisements encourage unhealthy eating habits.

10. Breakfast Chart · Three Cultures

Complete the chart using the textbook word bank. Add your own examples.

fried or scrambled eggs, bacon, toasts, cereals, bread and butter, cheese, sausages, roast or fried bread, baked beans, pancakes, tomatoes, mushrooms, waffles, coffee, milk

English breakfast
Moldovan breakfast
American breakfast

English: eggs, bacon, sausages, baked beans, tomatoes, mushrooms, toast, tea.
Moldovan: bread, cheese, eggs, porridge, tea or milk (examples vary).
American: pancakes, waffles, eggs, bacon, cereal, coffee or milk (examples vary).

There is no single compulsory answer: breakfast varies among families.

11. Writing · Chocolate Cookie Recipe

Study the recipe. Click any word in the ingredients or instructions to see RO/RU translations and hear it. Arrange the instructions in logical order. Write a similar recipe used in your country and present it to classmates.

Ingredients from the textbook

½ cup unsweetened cocoa powder; 1 cup white granulated sugar; ½ cup melted butter; 3 tablespoons vegetable oil; 1 egg; 2 teaspoons pure vanilla extract; 1⅓ cups all-purpose flour (or plain flour); ½ teaspoon baking powder; ½ teaspoon salt; ⅓ cup semi-sweet chocolate chips (add more if desired).

Order the instructions

Write your own recipe

Include the name, ingredients and at least four clear instructions. Use sequencing words: First, Next, Then, Finally.

FRUIT SALAD

Ingredients:

  • 2 apples
  • 2 bananas
  • 2 oranges
  • 1 cup of grapes
  • 2 tablespoons of natural yoghurt (optional)
Instructions:
  1. First, wash the apples and grapes carefully.
  2. Next, peel the bananas and oranges.
  3. Then, cut all the fruit into small pieces.
  4. Put the fruit in a large bowl and mix gently.
  5. Add the yoghurt if you like.
  6. Finally, serve the fruit salad fresh.
